correctness.rationale: The unique alternating two-cycle is solved exactly as u=lambda/(1+lambda), -u with Im(u)=0.5 tan(pi p/q)>0; the other symbolic two-step branches have no primitive two-cycle. Induction of affine branches yields necessary and sufficient q strict half-plane inequalities. Their normals are equal-distance root-of-unity cosets, disjoint for q divisible by 4 and identical for q congruent 2 mod 4. This proves the regular q-gon versus q/2-gon dichotomy, exact inradius and area. The two-step multiplier lambda squared has order q/2 and the map exchanges disjoint components, giving least periods 2 and q. All quantifiers, boundaries, and tie conventions are explicit. A standalone checker passes 63 finite numerical parameter pairs, not used as proof.

originality.rationale: The exact infinite even-denominator alternating-island polygon classification is not implied by either the general q-side upper bound or the coprime-cycle geometry theorems. For these cells component period ell=2 shares a factor with every even q. In contrast to the known q-gon case when gcd(ell,q)=1, the q=4k+2 case has a regular q/2-gon, e.g. pentagon for q=10, with explicit area and periods. The originating and older primary source were compared by mathematical implication, and known q=4,6 special examples are credited rather than asserted novel. Equivalent unindexed formulations remain possible.
residual_risks: No exhaustive bibliographic priority proof; an unindexed equivalent calculation for all even denominators may exist.
Outer billiards and bang-bang recurrences may encode the same family in different coordinates.
The two classical small-denominator polygon cases are already documented; novelty relies on the infinite q-mod-four theorem rather than those examples.

value.rationale: The regular-set component geometry of a known piecewise rotation is an intrinsic, motivated invariant. The exact parity-dependent halving q versus q/2 explains the role of failing the coprime-period hypothesis in prior polygon classification. It provides natural infinite families of regular odd-gon islands, exact areas, and dynamical period profiles, including q=10 pentagons. These are structural facts relevant to symbolic tiling and quantitative periodic islands, not arbitrary finite enumeration or a general theorem claimed without motivation.
